messages:
Alex C: heads up — after the FP8 rollout to canary yesterday I'm seeing a weird tail-latency bump on long contexts (>512). Per-token p50 is fine but p95/p99 jumps ~2.3x after token ~512. anyone else?
Mira P: saw something similar on my workload. do you have kernel counters/session logs?
Alex C: digging now. initial profiler shows frequent kernel fallback from the fused fp8-attn kernel to a slower path when seq_len crosses 512. counters show kernel_select: fp8_fused 53%, fp8_fallback 47% on affected traces.
Samir K: are those traces with big KV cache usage? sometimes cache fragmentation forces re-calc for some chunks which triggers different kernel selection.
Alex C: yes, most of the high-latency traces have high cache hit ratio overall but a bunch of mid-query misses during generation. interestingly the misses line up with the fallback events.
Rachael L: can you paste the exact kernel counter dump and a minimal perf trace?
Alex C: here are the snippets: 
```
kernel_counters {
  seq_len: 768
  selected_kernel: "fp8_fallback"
  fp8_fused_time_ms: 2.1
  fp8_fallback_time_ms: 6.4
  kv_cache_hits: 78.4
  kv_cache_evictions: 3
  batch_size: 8
}
trace_token_breakdown: [0.9, 0.8, 0.85, 0.82, 6.2, 6.4, 6.1]
```
Mira P: that trace_token_breakdown is classic: a stable fast plateau then a jump to the fallback kernel. looks like an alignment/tiling rule in kernel selector.
Samir K: what does the kernel selector config look like? any sequence-length thresholds wired to 512/768?
Alex C: selector: 
```
- candidate: fp8_fused
  max_seq: 512
- candidate: fp8_fallback
  supported_dtypes: [fp8, float16]
```
So yes, naive max_seq threshold. probably ok for small batches but with KV cache layout the effective chunk is bigger.
Rachael L: is batching heuristic merging partial prefix+generation segments incorrectly so seq_len estimate is off? batcher logs?
Alex C: batcher snapshots show grouping by request seq_len at enqueue, but we later append cached tokens which increase runtime seq for some sharded workloads. batcher doesn't currently recompute selector input after cache-aware concatenation.
Mira P: that means our selector is using pre-cache seq_len and decides fp8_fused, but at runtime the appended KV pages push it over the kernel's supported tile which triggers fallback.
Samir K: two quick mitigations: 1) move kernel selection after prefix concat (cheap) 2) relax fused kernel's max_seq threshold + add a fast path for partial tiles.
Alex C: agree. also seeing quant calibration impacts: when we use the new per-channel FP8 calibration the fallback rate drops by ~12% but top-1 quality regresses slightly on certain prompts. might need mixed-precision guardrails.
Rachael L: can you paste the cal reports? curious on scale factors and dynamic range skew.
Alex C: 
```
calibration_report: {
  method: "per-channel-fp8"
  overflow_pct: 0.02
  scale_median: 0.87
  scale_iqr: 0.14
  perf_delta: -6% (tokens/sec)
  fallback_rate: 0.35 -> 0.23
}
```
Mira P: tradeoff noted: fewer fallbacks but slower tokens/sec overall due to extra cast ops in mixed path? surprising that tokens/sec dropped.
Samir K: perf_delta could be from extra accumulation/quant-dequant ops if we change quant pipeline. need microbenchmarks for conv/gemm kernels with this calibration.
Alex C: I ran microbench: fp8 matmul perf is good when fused, but the new per-channel quant step adds a precompute scale multiply at runtime for some ops (we didn't hoist it). hooking scale hoist reduced the perf delta to -1.2%.
Rachael L: great. for observability we should add a per-token tag: kernel_used, cache_hit, calibration_version. then we can correlate quality/regression to exact token events.
Samir K: +1. also record "selector_decision_seq_len" and "runtime_seq_len" so we can detect mismatches that cause fallback.
Alex C: I'll open a small perf task: change selector position, hoist scale multiplies, add per-token telemetry, and a canary test with the fp8 per-channel cal.
Alex C: task: https://jira.redwood/PRODINF/3221 (will link PR once ready)
perf-bot: Canary results uploaded: canary=fp8-perchannel-2026-03-17, throughput_change=-1.1%, p95_latency_change=+12%, fallback_rate_down=11%
Mira P: p95 +12% is concerning. where is the p95 spike coming from — fallback mismatches or calibration overhead?
Alex C: looking at token tags, p95 spikes align with rare evictions that cause cache rehydration plus selector mismatch (runtime_seq_len > selected_kernel.max_seq). so both.
Rachael L: proposed rollout plan: 1) back out per-channel by default, keep as opt-in; 2) land selector-after-concat + telemetry; 3) hoist cal scales; 4) run 48h canary and monitor per-token p99 and kernel counters; 5) if p99 stable, flip on default.
Samir K: add automated alert: if fallback_rate increases >5% or p95 increases >8% within 24h, auto-rollback.
Alex C: done. PR incoming in a few hours. ping me if you want to pair on the selector change.
Rachael L: I'll review the PR and help with canary dashboard panels (per-token kernel heatmap + cache-hit waterfall).
Alex C: thanks team. low-churn followups: we should also add a small perf test that fuzzes cache alignment (prefix lengths 1..1024) to exercise selector heuristics.
Mira P: good call. that'll find the boundary conditions.
deploy-bot: deploy queued for staging: ref=fp8-selector-fix, owner=Alex C
Alex C: staging will run nightly perf suite. will post results here. :ear_of_rice:
